target: def Target : Prop := ∀ T : Set Form, Def15 T (neg (ex 1 (K Def17)))
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is the proposition that for every set T of formulas, with no hypotheses on T (in particular, even for the empty set), the formula ¬∃x₁ K(∀x₀ (K(¬R₀(x₀,x₀)) ↔ R₀(x₁,x₀))) is derivable from T. Here R₀(a,b) denotes the atom with relation index 0 and arguments a and b. The existential binds x₁ across the outer K, and the universal binds x₀ on both sides of the biconditional. A derivation may use members of T but need not use any. It may also use A or K(A) as an axiom whenever A is a closed formula obtained from a Def11 axiom by zero or more universal generalizations. The only inference rule in the derivation is modus ponens."}
translation: Target is the proposition that for every set T of formulas, with no hypotheses on T (in particular, even for the empty set), the formula ¬∃x₁ K(∀x₀ (K(¬R₀(x₀,x₀)) ↔ R₀(x₁,x₀))) is derivable from T. Here R₀(a,b) denotes the atom with relation index 0 and arguments a and b. The existential binds x₁ across the outer K, and the universal binds x₀ on both sides of the biconditional. A derivation may use members of T but need not use any. It may also use A or K(A) as an axiom whenever A is a closed formula obtained from a Def11 axiom by zero or more universal generalizations. The only inference rule in the derivation is modus ponens.

divergences.description: The scope is restricted as advertised: Lean states the diagonal instance with p(x) = ¬U(x,x) and U fixed to the binary relation symbol at index 0. It does not state the schema in p or allow U to stand for an arbitrary two-variable formula of arithmetic.

judgement.summary: For the claimed instance, the quantifiers, both occurrences of K, and the negation have exactly the source’s intended scopes. Requiring every T to prove the negation is equivalent to refuting the sentence in the base logic: T may be empty, and adding hypotheses preserves the derivation.
